head: pr17399-r3
report:
I found two defects the author should fix before merge. The first I reproduced; the second comes from reading the code and I did not run it. I spent about 20 minutes on a 9.7k-line diff, so the review is not exhaustive. I did not finish checking the cache-warmer's captured `fetch`, every request producer in `coding-agent`, or the provider stream watchdogs. ## 1. A request held by `/pause` keeps its provider in-flight slot, which blocks other omp processes for the whole pause **Mechanism.** In `packages/ai/src/stream.ts`, `withProviderInFlightLimit` now runs `await acquireProviderInFlightSlot(...)` first and `await holdBeforeDispatch(hold, options?.signal)` after it. The code comment says this order is deliberate ("Last, so the slot wait above cannot outlast it"). The slot is a cross-process lease on the filesystem, kept alive by heartbeats. `/pause` only affects one process, because `agentPauseGate` is a process singleton. So any request that reaches this point while the process is paused takes a lease and then sits on it until a human resumes. That includes titles, compaction, memory, judge calls, `/btw`, sharpshooter and cache-warm replays, which now all carry `agentPauseGate.dispatchHold(...)`. With `providers.

.maxConcurrency = N`, N such requests take every slot. Every other omp process using that provider then stalls behind them, even though it is not paused. Before this change, the pause stopped work at the agent-loop boundary, before any slot was taken. **Trigger.** Configure `maxInFlightRequests: { tests: 1 }`. Start request A with a `beforeDispatch` that never resolves, which stands in for a paused process. Then start request B with no hold, which stands in for another process sharing the cap. **Measured.** Probe: `scratch/control__pr17399-r3__t2/slot.test.ts`, run from `packages/ai`. ``` B finished while A held? false after ms: undefined B finished after resume at ms: 1555 ``` B ran only after A's hold was released. A held request should give up its slot, or the hold should run before the slot is acquired. If the hold has to stay last, the slot needs to be acquired again after the hold returns. ## 2. A TTS request waiting out `/pause` fails after 60 seconds instead of waiting **Mechanism.** In `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/tts.ts`, `synthesizeCloud` now passes `fetch: pauseHeldFetch(ctx.fetch ?? fetch)`. Inside `postSpeechRequest` (`packages/ai/src/speech/transport.ts`), `AbortSignal.timeout(60_000)` is merged into `signal` before `fetchImpl` is called. `pauseHeldFetch` then calls `agentPauseGate.dispatchHold(signal)`, and that wait ends when the signal aborts. So the 60-second deadline counts down during the pause, and the hold rejects with `TimeoutError` (`throwIfAborted()` after `waitUntilResumed`). The tool call fails rather than waiting for the resume. This contradicts the new doc text in `docs/slash-command-internals.md`: "A request's own deadline starts after the hold, so pausing before a side request begins cannot fail it". Image generation, commit inference, text summary and auto-repair all wait out the pause before arming their deadlines (`await agentPauseGate.dispatchHold(signal)()`). TTS does not. **Trigger.** Run the cloud `tts` tool (an OpenAI-speech or xAI-TTS model). Engage `/pause` after the tool starts and before its POST goes out, for example while the API key resolves, and keep it paused for more than 60 seconds. The tool fails with a timeout, and no request is sent after the resume. **Fix.** Wait out the pause before `synthesizeSpeech` is called, as `image-gen.ts` does. Alternatively, arm the speech timeout after the fetch-level hold. ## 3. Low: `wrapTransport` / `TransportWrapper` is new public API that nothing in production uses This is dead weight in the patch rather than a correctness bug. The diff adds `StreamOptions.wrapTransport`, the `TransportWrapper` type, and the "live build" machinery in `transport-fetch.ts` (`live`, `layerWrapper`, in-place `stamp.holds.push`). A search outside the tests finds no caller of `wrapTransport`. All of that state and its long contract docs are carried and exercised only by tests. The in-place `holds.push` on a live build is also a way for holds to pile up on a shared fetch if it is ever reused. Drop this code until a caller exists, or land it together with that caller.
